questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I kind of picked at random. It was important for me to study at an english-speaking university. I was intrigued by the large selection of elective courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: My exchange took place during the covid-lockdowns of winter 2021-22. I would not recommend that experience. The university was in large part because of that not able to provide a welcoming experience for me, but it was worsened as their material was oriented towards welcoming long-term international students starting their first year of studies. I was, however, able to figure everything out in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little. I could read on their website and write emails. There was one virtual meetup for exchange students partway through the first month which allowed me to make some friends and from there we helped each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would recommend finding housing in the Plateau rather than Downtown. While it was easy getting to-from campus (I went to the Downtown Campus), prices, vibes, social life, events and grocery stores are much nicer up there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Montreal has very nice tenant laws; It is a good idea to get an official standard contract (if you're renting) and read it through, the rules are very clear and generous to tenants.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration process is very different from the one in KU, and you will not be able to apply without first getting special permission, so just write directly to professors or program directors for access. This is not something they told me was possible, but I had no issues at all. Also don't be afraid to use the waiting list options as many students switch classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just talk to someone directly, hopefully the student services will be in person when you go :)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got amazing classes! Don't be afraid to ask for permission to take 400-level courses, as they were in my experience much more engaging and had way smaller classes which was incredible

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As I wrote above ^

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I study anthropology, and the program is great for electives!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses varied wildly from course to course and subject to subject. At times, the very free and pick-your-own-path style of education in North America leads to frustrating repetitions and low baselines of common knowledge, but there is also way more interesting and niche courses to pick from.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Be aware that they teach differently, and I feel lucky to have had my first two years in Copenhagen. The students have in general never tried field work, and there was _a lot_ more writing than what I was used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTH 498-F - Special topics: Introduction to the Anthropocene
ANTH 498-G - Special topics: Militarization in Oceania
ANTH 343 - Media Ethnographies
ANTH 302 - Art, Aesthetics, and Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pick specific courses ("narrow" focus). General courses can get kind of lost at times.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I was not able to get a refund of the insurance cost even though I was entitled to it as a Danish citizen. The issue is that the processing of the application (which was embarrasingly complex) took 90+ days while the deadline from the time I was able to start applying was way shorter. Maybe you can make it work.

ALSO: Montreal still has issues with water lead contamination in certain places, make sure to find out if the place you stay has replaced their water pipes or you should probably buy a Brita water filter if you would prefer not to be exposed.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices were more or less the same, I just ended up spending more money than what I am used to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I loved the People's Potato (Free food program) and in general the vibrant culture of student organising and cooperatives at Concordia, including: The Farms at Loyola Campus, Le Frigo Vert and the Hive Café

Mostly I had to find things myself as most things were closed because of the covid lockdowns

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, I'm sure

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went for a bouldering membership at Café Bloc. It's expensive, but fun and very social.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go ice skating in the winter. Enjoy all the public exhibitions and performances at Place des Art. Go to pop-up markets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are pretty friendly,,, It was easy for me to adjust. Just very hard to adjust to the cold weather and the baffling tendency of people to not use blanket but instead just crank up the heat - whats up with that?

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No just be social. Don't look at your phone if you have noone to talk to: Eventually someone will pity you and come up to you

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was a shock to learn about the intense battle between Francophone and Anglophone visions of the Province.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There's a lot. I saw a lot of light/projection-oriented art and installations while there which I loved. I just love the diversity and intensity of the city in general. Also I like that theres a lot of bars that brew their own beer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Focus on making friends so you can hang out with someone daily – alienation and lonelyness are negative feedback loops. 

You don't have to do all the touristy things people talk about.

Try and talk with the professors, they are extremely kind and nice in my experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lockdowns – my bank account

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
